public_rationale: The statement supplies no competence threshold for “good,” scale boundary for “large-scale,” or test of what makes learning “vital” [marcus-three-ideas-from-linguistics-that-c4f7da-o1]. These definitions are needed to judge the proposed necessity. The study submitted January 23, 2020 examines scaling of language-model cross-entropy loss; it does not establish that every qualifying language system requires large-scale learning [e1].
limitations: The evidence does not establish that the proposed necessity is true or false.
Successful scaling within trained language models does not establish necessity across other approaches.
Without defined competence and learning-scale boundaries, a proposed counterexample cannot be classified consistently.

criteria.contradiction_condition: After those definitions are fixed, a system meeting the competence standard without the specified learning component would challenge necessity. The original wording does not determine whether a narrow-domain system qualifies.
